Bench: J.K. Maheshwari, Aravind Kumar

1
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Criminal Original Jurisdiction
 Transfer Petition (Criminal) No. 524 Of 2024
 Kavita Mohindroo & Anr.  Petitioners
 Versus
 State Of Uttarakhand & Anr.  Respondents
 O R D E R

1. Seeking transfer of Criminal Case No. 1582/2023 titled as State of Uttarakhand Vs. Tushar Mohindroo & Anr., from the Court of Judicial Magistrate, Almora, Uttarakhand to the court of the Judicial Magistrate, Gurugram, Haryana, the present transfer petition has been filed by the Mother-in-Law and the Husband.

sentences.text:
2. As conceded by the parties, the matter was referred to the Supreme Court Mediation Centre,
where the settlement agreement has been entered into between them.

The terms of the settlement are as under :
1. The Following settlement has been arrived at between the parties hereto.
i) That the first Party/husband and the Second party/wife have mutually reached an agreement Date: 2025.02.04 17:36:54 IST Reason:
to dissolve their marriage duly solemnised on 30.04.2021 by way of mutual consent divorce petition as per section 13-B of Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.
ii) That the parties declare that no issue/child was born bout of the said marriage/wedlock.

iii) That the parties have mutually agreed to settle all their claims and it is settled that the first party/husband will give a full and final amount of Rs,2,50,000/- (Rupees Two lacs fifty thousand only) (hereinafter referred to as the Settlement Amount) as full and final settlement amount towards any claims whatsoever, of the Second party.

sentences.text: That the Second Party has agreed that by way of the instant settlement, all her claims towards past, present and future maintenance / alimony, stridhan have been fully and finally settled and now there will be no claim left against the First Party or his family members, of any kind.

v) The parties undertake to file a joint application (hereinafter referred to as the said Application)
seeking divorce and quashing of all pending cases before the Honble Supreme Court of India (hereinafter referred to as the Honble Court) under Article 142 of the Constitution of India within two months of signing the settlement agreement.

During the course of this hearing wherein the Honble Court will grant divorce, and any other pending cases or complaints are being quashed, the First Party undertakes to pay the Second Party a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rs Fifty Thousand Only) at the time of signing the present agreement and a demand draft of Rs.2,00,000/- (Two lacs only)
before the Honble Court at the time of listing of application before the Honble Court.

vi) That in case, the Honble Court declines to either grant divorce or quash the FIR or Criminal Case, as the case may be, the parties agree to the following terms :
a.
That the first party and the Second party will jointly file a divorce petition under Section 13B of HMA, 1955 before the Ld. Family Courts, Gurugram, Haryana.

The First party undertakes to pay Rs.50,000/=- (Rupees fifty thousand only) to the Second party to pay Rs.50,000/- (Rupees fifty thousand only) to the Second party at the time of grant of divorce under Section 13B(2) of HMA, 1955.

b. That the first party undertakes to unconditionally withdraw case bearing No. HMA/1473/2022 filed under Section 9 of the HMA, 1955 instituted by him against the Second party,
before the Ld. Family Court, Gurugram, Haryana.

c. That the first party will file quashing petition U/s 528 of BNSS before the Honble Court of Uttarakhand, for quashing of FIR No. 6 dated 03.04.2023 U/s 323, 498A, 504, 506 of IPC and 3 & 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.

2. By signing this Agreement, the parties hereto state that they have no further claims or demands against each other and all the disputes and difference relating to their matrimony have been settled voluntarily by the parties hereto through the process of Mediation.
3. That in case of breach of any of the terms of the present settlement by any of the parties, the other party can seek such enforcement, as per law.

3. In furtherance, a sum of Rs.50,000/- was paid at the time of settlement and a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- has been paid by the Petitioner No. 2 (husband) to Respondent No.2 (wife) by way of three Demand Drafts bearing Nos. 247636, 247637 and 247638 dated 04.12.2024 drawn on HDFC Bank Ltd. Harsha Bhawan, Delhi amounting to Rs.1,00,000/-, Rs.50,000/- and Rs.50,000/-
respectively which she has accepted.

sentences.text: Petitioner No.2 and Respondent No.2 are present before this Court and they have been identified by their respective counsel.
We have interacted with them.
The have acknowledged the terms of the settlement.

5. In view of the settlement, it is jointly stated that the decree of divorce by mutual consent may be granted and the FIR No. 6 dated 03.04.2023 for the offences under Sections 323, 498A, 504, 506 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act registered at Women Police Station Almora, Uttarakhand may be directed to be quashed disposing all other pending cases putting a quietus to the litigation.
6.
In view of the foregoing, by the consent of both the parties, the present Transfer Petition stands disposed of with the following directions :
(i) As per the settlement, the amount, as specified therein has been paid by Petitioner No. 2 and duly accepted by the Respondent No. 2.
The parties state that they shall adhere to the terms of the settlement.

(ii) As prayed and agreed, FIR No. 6 dated 03.04.2023 for the offences under Sections 323, 498A, 504, 506 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act registered at Women Police Station Almora, Uttarakhand shall stand quashed.
(iii) All other proceedings pending between the parties in any Court shall be treated as disposed of in view of the order passed today by this Court.
(iv) As prayed by the parties, we exercise our jurisdiction under Article 142 of the Constitution and grant a decree of divorce by mutual consent.
Consequently, the marriage solemnised on 30.04.2021 between the Petitioner No. 2 husband (Tushar Mohindroo) and Respondent No. 2 wife (Swati Tewari) shall stand dissolved.
By an outcome of the dissolution of marriage, the parties are free to lead their lives separately as per their own will.
7. Registry is directed to draw a decree of divorce in the matter.
8. A copy of this order be sent to the courts concerned so that the cases may be closed and consigned.
9. Pending applications, if any, stand disposed of.

,J.
[J.K. MAHESHWARI] ,J.

[ARAVIND KUMAR] New Delhi;
